history.period: 19th century — founded 1840s; silver idol installed April 1843
history.summary: Built in the 1840s at a site where Hanuman was covertly worshipped: devotees had placed a picture of Hanuman at a fireworks shop during the more oppressive periods of Portuguese rule. In April 1843 the picture was replaced by a silver idol, and the business community of Mapusa raised funds to buy the shop and build the temple on its site. The temple is unusual in facing south (rare for temples), has a marble floor and carved teak woodwork on the north side, and houses idols of Rama and Sita besides Maruti. AMBIGUITY FLAG: the CSV name 'Hanuman Temple' is generic — this file documents the best-identified candidate, Shree Hanuman Maharudra Sansthan at 8/3 Hutatma Circle, the only Mapusa Hanuman temple with documented history; if the CSV meant a different neighbourhood shrine, reassign.

name: Shree Hanuman Maharudra Sansthan
town_description: Mapusa is Goa's third-largest town and the headquarters of Bardez taluka in North Goa, about 13 km from Panaji. It is chiefly a market town serving the northern beaches, famous for its Friday weekly market, and has few tourist sites beyond its Hanuman temple, municipal buildings on Altinho hillock and the Church of Our Lady of Miracles.
